ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, general partners, and beneficial owners against the OFAC SDN list, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (including restrictive measures against Russia/Belarus), Luxembourg FIU instructions, and local competent authority CNS/register lists. Enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons (PEPs) for at least 12 months after leaving office, with ongoing transaction monitoring and periodic re-screening at least every 90 business days.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) portal at www.lbr.lu (RCS lookup and name reservation module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be entered in Luxembourgish, French, German, English, or a language using the Latin alphabet; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters for registration. The name must be capable of distinguishing the entity from all other registered legal persons and must not contravene public policy or Good moral. The statutory suffix 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' must appear in the legal name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a reasoned decision from the RCS Registrar. The applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar within 8 days of the rejection, providing evidence of distinctiveness and compliance. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may appeal to the Luxembourg Tribunal de l'Entreprise (Commercial Chamber) within one month of notification, using a Luxembourg lawyer; the court may order registration within a specified deadline.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an SCSp provided the registered office is a physical address in Luxembourg where administrative formalities, supervisory authorities, and correspondence can be served; a self-contained virtual-office service is accepted where the domiciliation agent maintains full statutory records and provides remote access. No active economic activity requirement applies at pre-incorporation, but substance expectations increase if the entity holds Luxembourg tax rulings or undertakes finance activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for passive holding SCSp: approximately 5% annualized unannounced on-site inspection probability. For distribution of simulated social casino games via Apple/Google IAP without a gaming license, the risk remains moderate (10%–15%) due to AML/CFT supervision and consumer-protection scrutiny by the Luxembourgish regulators where relevant; only the postal/domiciliation service address is inspected, not a trading premises.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Articles 101-1 et seq. on Special Limited Partnerships (SCSp)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Charter (statuts) of the Special Limited Partnership filed with the RCS via the e-justice portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum capital requirement for SCSp; contributions may be in cash, in kind, or in industry; no escrow account mandated
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp) contemplated hereby is duly formed under Luxembourg law, and the initial capital subscriptions of the limited partner are accepted. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Partnership shall be established at the address set forth in the Charter; and that [Name] is hereby appointed General Partner and [Name] is appointed Managing Partner, each with full and unconditional authority to execute all filings, engage counsel, open bank accounts, obtain tax and VAT identifications, and undertake any measure necessary for registration, licensing, and lawful commencement of business. This resolution is effective immediately and until revoked in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary or licensed legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Luxembourg-law charter of the Special Limited Partnership. Have all initial partners execute the charter in accordance with the law. If a corporate body acts as general partner, hold a board meeting to approve the charter and capital subscription. Notarization is not compulsory but may be obtained for evidentiary certainty.
required_dossiers: Bank account confirmation for initial contribution (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resubmit the corrected charter upon curing any ambiguity or legally inadequate provision; a notarial re-execution may be required if the registry so demands.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via rcs.lu or guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the registration application with the RCS, attaching the executed charter, powers of attorney, and supporting identification documents. Pay the statutory filing fee and request publication of the formation notice in the Official Gazette of Luxembourg (RESA).
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for the filer
Identity documents of general partner and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, cure the specifically stated deficiencies within one calendar month; alternatively, file a formal request for rectification with the RCS registry office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Administration des contributions directes (ACD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit tax registration forms to obtain the Luxembourg VAT number and establish files for corporate income tax and municipal business tax. Declare the intended business activity, namely publishing of simulated social casino and virtual slots games.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct the omitted information or respond to the tax administration's request within the prescribed period; procedural remedy may be lodged by written explanation or administrative appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp as an employer with the CCSS if any natural person will be hired. Submit the registration form and obtain the employer number for social security contribution payments. If no employees are initially engaged, this step may be deferred but remains mandatory before onboarding staff.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend and resubmit incomplete declarations; confirm effective insurance coverage retroactively if required by the CCSS.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and AML/KYC clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Luxembourg credit institution and CSSF-supervised financial service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Luxembourg business bank account by submitting the complete KYC/AML file of all partners and the beneficial owners. Provide proof of source of funds and demonstrate the intended use of Apple IAP and Google Play Billing payment rails. The account is needed to operationalize contributions and administrative expenses.
required_dossiers: Passports or identity cards of all beneficial owners
Source of funds and wealth documentation
Schematic business plan and game distribution overview
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank issues an adverse decision, provide the additional KYC evidence requested or apply to an alternative licensed banking institution with a reinforced compliance file.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) and Institut Luxembourgeois de la Normalisation (ILNAS)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial or gaming operating license required for simulated social casino publishing; general RCS registration and standard business compliance are sufficient

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (software/office activity, no physical industrial installation)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; zero industrial discharge expected. General EU environmental standards for waste electrical equipment and energy efficiency apply to IT equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification required from the Grand Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) for any office premises; workplace safety inspection by Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for occupational compliance; structural load certification not applicable for standard office software development.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct/income tax, with centralised administrative portal at guichet.lu; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT/turnover tax and registration; business registration through the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) maintained by Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SCSp, the contract under Luxembourg law must be filed with the RCS. After incorporation, the entity receives a 13-digit national identification number (matricule / LLN) used for tax purposes. The SCSp, as a fiscally transparent partnership, is not typically subject to Luxembourg CIT on its own income, but must still register with the ACD and AED where it carries on taxable activities. Foreign founders without EU/EEA establishment may need to appoint a Luxembourg tax representative. VAT identification is obtained by filing the standard VAT registration application through the AED/guichet.lu portal, supported by the partnership deed, proof of address, partners' identification, and a description of the proposed electronic-services activity. Registration for employer withholding, VAT, and indirect-tax returns is undertaken through MyGuichet; the custom/matricule reference links all administrative filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible (SCSp is fiscally transparent; Luxembourg income tax is imposed on each partner/sociétaire at partner level, subject to hybrid-mismatch recharacterisation in cross-border settings).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Luxembourg partnerships, including certain SCS/SCSp forms, may elect to be treated as subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (optant partnerships) if the partnership satisfies statutory conditions, including, where applicable, publication of audited financial statements and partner composition requirements. The transparent regime is default; partners may elect, directly or indirectly, to file and pay at the partnership level for administrative convenience, but this does not derogate from the pass-through classification unless the opt-in corporate-taxation conditions are met. ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules apply to foreign-electronic-commerce and publishing structures where another jurisdiction treats an SCSp as a corporation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No minimum turnover threshold for non-established taxable persons making Luxembourg taxable supplies; any such supply triggers VAT registration unless covered by OSS or the €10,000 EU distance-sale/electronically-supplied-services threshold. A resident small-business exemption applies to established businesses with annual Luxembourg turnover not exceeding EUR 35,000, subject to the AED's rules and anti-avoidance limitations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, API-based e-invoicing authorisation, or digital stamping is currently in force in Luxembourg. e-Invoicing is permitted and, in B2G supplies, mandatory under EU Directive 2014/55/EU using structured formats compliant with EN 16931/Peppol. For this simulated-social-casino/publishing activity, no special Luxembourg clearance platform is required; Apple IAP and Google Play Billing must follow EU e-commerce VAT marketplace rules, and the platform may be regarded as the deemed supplier for B2C digital-service supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical exports of goods to non-EU destinations may be zero-rated provided the Executive VAT Directive criteria are met, including actual removal from EU customs territory, transfer of ownership/export title, and preservation of export evidence. Pure digital-services exports (simulated casino slots publishing) are governed by place-of-supply rules: B2C supplies to Luxembourg consumers are taxable at 17%; B2B supplies to non-Luxembourg EU customers are reverse-charged; B2C supplies to non-EU customers are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT (customer-local VAT applies), not strictly an export zero-rating. Zero-rating is also available for certain services directly related to goods export or cross-border intangible services if contractually and factually supplied for purposes outside the EU.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/EX-A or electronic declaration through Luxembourg PLDA/National Customs System)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing actual departure from EU territory
Commercial Invoice containing the full consignee's details, Incoterms, quantity, description and value
Proof of export such as an exit summary declaration, external transit (T1) document, or customs-output confirmation from the member state of exit
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/payment settlement evidence showing the foreign customer's payment
Transport and insurance documentation supporting the physical movement where goods are exported
Intrastat declaration where applicable for intra-EU dispatches, and OSS/VAT e-commerce summaries for cross-border B2C supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED may reopen and audit export zero-rating for up to 5 years (extended to 10 years in fraud or intentional failure cases). If export evidence is incomplete or the transaction is recharacterised as domestic or intra-EU, 17% VAT becomes immediately payable, with statutory late interest, administrative fines, and retroactive correction of refunds. Intentional false zero-rating or fraudulent export claims expose the SCSp, tax representative if any, and responsible partners/managers to criminal sanctions, including fines up to double the evaded tax and imprisonment for tax offences. Abuse-of-law doctrines under Luxembourg case law and EU anti-fraud principles disallow artificial routing of digital gaming/revenue streams through Luxembourg where no real establishment or economic substance exists; penalties may include denial of exemption, clawback of input VAT credits, and deregistration for non-compliance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB); the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises credit institutions and EMIs.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is part of the euro area; the euro is freely convertible for all current and capital transactions under Articles 63–65 TFEU. There are no exchange-control restrictions on profit remittances, loan repayments, or equity distributions. The SCSp, while lacking separate legal personality under Luxembourg law, is recognised for banking purposes as an account-holding arrangement and contracts through its general partner. Remittances to non-resident partners are not subject to any prior BCL approval; only statistical reporting duties and standard AML/CFT obligations apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg and EU law impose no mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds. Export revenues from digital gaming can be retained in EUR or any convertible currency; there is no requirement to repatriate or convert into EUR within a statutory period.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility for EU/EEA-authorised electronic money institutions (EMIs) that hold a valid passport under PSD2 into Luxembourg; these can provide multi-currency IBANs, local clearing, and e-money wallets. Offshore (non-EU) EMIs have low viability because they lack the EU passport and are treated as unregulated counterparties by Luxembourg banks and the CSSF. Legal constraints: the SCSp must be the account holder; the EMI must verify the SCSp's existence via the RCS; social-casino activity is often restricted under EMI internal risk policies due to perceived 'gambling' adjacency; a legal opinion on the non-gambling nature of the social-casino model is generally required.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, a physical onboarding interview is mandatory at most tier-1 banks for a non-regulated SCSp with non-resident partners; at least one authorised signatory (usually the general partner representative) must appear at the bank's Luxembourg office with original identification and corporate documents. Remote opening is permitted only after the physical meeting and completion of eIDAS electronic signature steps; full video-only onboarding is rarely available for this legal form. If the general partner is itself a regulated EU entity (e.g., a Luxembourg management company), a remote video interview may be accepted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity of the multi-tiered SCSp structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current RCS extract; notarised partnership agreement; share-of-beneficial-ownership schedule; identity and address verification for all natural-person UBOs; declaration from the general partner on source of partnership assets; UBO register (RBE) submission receipt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk sector classification: simulated social casino and virtual slots activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent Luxembourg law firm legal opinion confirming the absence of a gambling licence requirement and the non-real-money nature of the model; certified press/terms of use proving that virtual chips have no cash-out value; age-verification and geolocation controls; transaction-monitoring policy for high-velocity micropayments.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No demonstrated operating history or audited financial statements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved business plan with 3-year financial projections; executed LOIs/term sheets with major app-store platforms; evidence of committed initial capital in a funded escrow; banker's references from the UBO's primary bank; audited parent-company accounts if a parent exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs domiciled in lower-risk but high-volume jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport and notarised power of attorney; official address proof; tax residence certificates; declaration confirming no politically exposed person (PEP) status; independent AML background check report; bank statements for the last 6–12 months clearly tracing source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected chargeback ratio or refund reversals from app-store merchants
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chargeback tracking and mitigation policy; technical refund-control SOPs; merchant account performance summary; projected chargeback ratio under the acquiring bank's limits; optional voluntary excess reserve balance to cover potential reversals.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital subscriptions from non-resident partners must be credited via SWIFT MT103 from the remitting bank. The wire must reference the Luxembourg interbank BIC and the SCSp's account number. The bank requires a capital-call notice, the relevant excerpt of the partnership agreement, and an AML/source-of-funds statement to process the transfer. Purpose code under Luxembourg balance-of-payments statistical reporting should be 'Equity capital contribution – participation in partnerships' (direct investment category) as instructed by the bank. If the capital remains below prevailing notifiable thresholds, no prior BCL approval is required; the bank, as reporting agent, will capture the transaction automatically.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For verified, arm's-length commercial payments, the primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for cross-border EUR/USD transfers and SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA CT) for euro-denominated EU beneficiary settlements. Apple/Google platform disbursements are processed via merchant wallet payouts or SWIFT MT103 to the SCSp's collection account. For physical-goods licensing distribution, a documentary commercial LC facility can be established via the relationship bank, using SWIFT MT700/707 messaging. SEPA Instant Credit Transfer is available for intra-EU beneficiary accounts that hold sufficient liquidity thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable outright forwards (standard one-month to one-year tenors)
EUR/USD cross-currency swaps under ISDA 2002 with CSA collateral terms
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-fully-convertible emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, BRL) booked through authorised Luxembourg credit institutions
FX vanilla options (EUR calls/puts on USD, EUR calls on GBP/CHF) under ISDA/CSA

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within one month following the anniversary of the initial or last confirmed UBO filing; any transfer of SCSp interests must be reported within one month of transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine of EUR 500 to EUR 1,250 per offence; repeated failure may be published in the RBE and trigger forced administrative correction; late confirmation is treated as non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements / annual accounts deposit (if not exempt; alternatively retain statutory exemption analysis)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the SCSp to judicial formal notice, coercive daily penalty (astreinte), criminal fine of EUR 500 to EUR 25,000, and possible court-ordered strike-off from the RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg income tax / partnership information return (déclaration fiscale) where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, return is generally due by 31 December of the following year; electronic filing extensions are at ACD discretion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 0.6% per month on assessed tax; late-filing fine up to EUR 25,000; risk of estimated assessment and fiscal penalties if the return is omitted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual internal statutory-register audit and partner register reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General partner / registered agent; records must be made available to Luxembourg Business Registers and RBE authorities on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Conducted at least annually before the UBO confirmation anniversary and simultaneous with the annual accounts approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective registers prejudice the legal presumption of ownership and can trigger penalties under the commercial register and AML laws; failure to produce records to authorities is a separate offense

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) applies if the SCSp exceeds two of three medium-enterprise thresholds: balance sheet total > EUR 20,000,000; net turnover > EUR 40,000,000; average staff > 250; audit also required if the SCSp is a regulated fund, public-interest entity, or the partnership agreement so provides
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts; IFRS permitted for consolidated accounts; the SCSp is fiscally transparent and its accounting must nonetheless be kept by the general partner in accordance with the partnership agreement

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must confirm the accuracy of beneficial-owner data at least once every 12 months, normally within one month of the anniversary of the initial RBE declaration; each transfer of an SCSp interest must be documented in the partner register and filed with the RBE within one month; the annual confirmation must be completed even when no transfer has occurred
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members / SCSp partners register (capital contributions, economic shares, and transfer history)
Register of Directors / general partner governance records (for a corporate general partner)
Minute Book (general partner resolutions, partner meetings, and written consents)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 30,000 per annum, where a statutory audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% entity-level CIT for SCSp (fiscally transparent); corporate partners are subject to Luxembourg CIT at 17% (15% base + 7% unemployment surcharge) plus municipal business tax of approximately 6.75% in Luxembourg City, yielding aggregate effective headline rate of 22.80%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to SCSp or social casino gaming. The transparent regime eliminates SCSp-level CIT. Corporate partners may apply the participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying dividends/capital gains) if holding conditions are met. Qualifying software IP income may benefit from an 80% exemption under the Luxembourg IP box regime, but social casino app income must be independently tested for eligible IP asset status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1001 (Corporate Income Tax Return) via Luxembourg eTax / MyGuichet.lu; SCSp generally files an informational partnership declaration showing allocation of taxable result to partners. Non-resident corporate partners with a Luxembourg PE file Form 1002.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; the tax year is the calendar year unless an approved different fiscal period is adopted.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed by 31 May following the tax year-end; e-filed returns receive an automatic extension to 30 June, and the Luxembourg tax administration ordinarily grants further extension to 31 December upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp name, RCS number, Luxembourg tax number, registered office, VAT number and legal form.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners must state the Luxembourg PE address and insert the SCSp's RCS legal identifier as the PE reference.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial income computed under Article 114 LIR, adjusted for non-deductible expenses, provisions and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a transparent SCSp, report only the pro-rata taxable profit attributable to the Luxembourg PE of the non-resident partner; do not include worldwide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit subject to Luxembourg municipal business tax; for Luxembourg City the rate is approximately 6.75%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: SCSp profits of the Luxembourg PE are fully exposed to municipal tax; the SCSp itself is not assessed, but corporate partners receive the allocation on a look-through basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for 100% relief on qualifying dividends and capital gains under the Luxembourg participation exemption (Article 166 LIR).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only available to a corporate partner that itself satisfies Luxembourg holding thresholds and subject-to-tax requirements; no exemption at the SCSp level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward from prior tax years, subject to statutory restriction and anti-abuse rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the transparent SCSp flow through to partner level and are usable only by each partner under its domestic loss-offset rules; the SCSp cannot aggregate or shelter losses in a separate entity.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a fixed penalty up to EUR 1,500 per return plus overdue interest at 2.5% p.a., rising to 5.25% for fraudulent default. Continued failure can produce an administrative penalty of 10% of the underpaid tax, and intentional misdeclaration exposes the signatory to criminal fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% is the statutory dividend withholding tax for Luxembourg stock corporations, but an SCSp distribution of profits is not treated as a dividend under domestic law because the SCSp is fiscally transparent. Consequently, no Luxembourg dividend WHT is imposed on partner profit allocations unless the SCSp is recharacterised as opaque or conversions create deemed dividend treatment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because SCSp profit allocations are not subject to withholding at source, treaty relief is not ordinarily required. Where a corporate partner is taxable and a withholding obligation arises from an opaque disposition, Luxembourg procedure requires submission of Form 1002/T to the Luxembourg administration, accompanied by the partner's tax residence certificate (TRC) proving beneficial ownership and satisfaction of the ATAD/beneficial-owner anti-abuse conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Luxembourg WHT on interest and royalties is generally 0%; the principal exception relates to certain savings or asset-backed structures. Under most Luxembourg DTTs, interest and royalties are exempt from Luxembourg source WHT (0%), while deemed dividends paid by a recharacterised entity may attract a 5% or 10% treaty rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File is mandatory for groups with consolidated turnover of EUR 750,000,000 or more. Local File is required when cross-border controlled transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 per tax year in aggregate; lower thresholds apply to financial transactions and intangibles. Even below these limits, a taxpayer must maintain contemporaneous economic substance evidence to refute recharacterisation.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR). Instead, courts and tax authorities enforce a substance-over-form doctrine, beneficial ownership requirements, anti-hybrid rules and an ATAD-based General Anti-Abuse Rule (GAAR). A SCSp must demonstrate real physical substance, effective senior management in Luxembourg, meaningful payroll, bona fide commercial decision-making and consistent bank account flows to sustain transparent tax treatment and DTA protection. Social casino and virtual slots gaming requires no gambling licence in Luxembourg, but substance and AML compliance are mandatory.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Misuse of SCSp Transparency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate underreporting of income, falsification of partnership books, sham cost deductions, withholding material profit allocations from the tax return, or using a shell SCSp to house third-party gaming revenues without any operational reality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A retroactive 10-year assessment window, late interest up to 5.25% p.a., fixed penalties up to EUR 1,500, a 10% administrative penalty on evaded tax, criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and commercial representatives may be jointly and severally liable for restitution of unpaid tax; authorities can obtain travel bans, asset seizures, professional disqualification and imprisonment where the SCSp veil is pierced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Shell Company / Insufficient Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Luxembourg registered office without employees, management minutes or decision-making capacity, routing in-app payments through non-resident merchant processors, and claiming treaty or transparency benefits while having no active gaming operation in Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of the SCSp's transparent character; recharacterisation as an opaque Luxembourg resident company subject to 22.80% effective CIT plus municipal tax, net wealth tax, VAT and 10-year back assessment; denial of DTA benefits and cancellation of tax rulings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, statutory managers and partners who knowingly cause or permit the artificial arrangement may be named co-taxpayers; Luxembourg courts allow veil piercing, civil restitution, freezing orders and travel bans in abuse-of-law cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT and Simulated Gambling Payment Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting virtual currency or in-app payments from unverified users, using hot/cold wallets to obscure payment trails, omitting AML/KYC controls, or routing merchant settlement through unrelated third-party PSPs before profit distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg AML law authorises administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover for serious, repeated or systematic breaches; criminal money-laundering penalties include fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years, plus confiscation of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML officers, directors and shadow managers face personal criminal liability, passport seizures, travel restrictions and civil damages; the Luxembourg financial regulator may also ban the individual from managing regulated payment or fintech entities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Hidden Permanent Establishment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inflating intra-group royalties for software licences, paying excessive management fees to foreign affiliates, allocating all profit outside Luxembourg while retaining only a zero-risk SCSp title, or exercising substantive management offshore through parallel decision-making.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax authorities may adjust transfer prices to arm's length, impose a 5%-10% late-payment penalty, add interest at 5.25% p.a., and assert a deemed Luxembourg PE, triggering CIT, municipal tax and up to five years of retroactive assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve artificial intercompany pricing or negligently ignore economic substance may be liable for restitution to co-partners and to the tax administration; personal travel bans and imprisonment are reserved for evidence of fraudulent misconduct.
